title: Reservation domain model
idea: The domain model separates the fixed floor plan (Restaurant, Table) from bookings in time (TimeSlot, Reservation), and links each Reservation to one Customer and one Table.

analogy.text: A floor plan pinned on the wall and the host's booking book. The plan rarely changes; the book gains a new line for every party and evening.
analogy.breaks: The book cannot spot a clash; TimeSlot.overlaps can, and page 3 refuses it.

points: A Restaurant owns its Tables and decides how long one seating lasts.
A Table has a capacity and an Area; it stores no booking state.
A TimeSlot is a half-open interval, so back-to-back seatings do not overlap.
A Reservation joins one Customer, one Table and one TimeSlot for a party size.

edges.label: has 1..*
edges.caption: A Restaurant owns one or more Tables. The list is copied, so callers cannot change it.

edges.label: in 1
edges.caption: Each Table sits in one Area. Customers may ask for the patio later.

edges.label: creates
edges.caption: Restaurant.slotAt turns a start time into a TimeSlot of the seating length.

edges.label: uses 1
edges.caption: A Reservation points at exactly one Table, and the party must fit its capacity.

edges.label: for 1
edges.caption: A Reservation covers one TimeSlot. Two on the same Table must not overlap.

edges.label: by 1
edges.caption: One Customer makes the Reservation. A Customer can hold many over time.

edges.label: has
edges.caption: ReservationStatus is an enum. Page 4 turns it into a state machine.

code.title: The model in Java 17
code.caption: Records for fixed data, a class for Reservation because its status changes. Invariants live in constructors.

walk.text: One restaurant with three tables and a 90-minute seating, plus one customer.
Build three slots and test two overlaps: back-to-back and one hour apart.
A party of three fits the four-seat table T2.
Two bad inputs are refused: a party too big and a zero-length slot.
Half-open overlap: each slot must start before the other one ends.
The restaurant owns the seating length, so every slot has the same rule.
The constructor checks the party fits the table before any field is set.

pitfalls: Do not store booked times on Table; one Table serves many reservations a night.
Use half-open intervals, or a 20:30 finish blocks a 20:30 start.
Validate party size in the Reservation constructor, not in every caller.

quiz.q: What does the second line of DomainModel print?
options: rejected: slot must end after it starts
quiz.why: Slot c starts at 20:00, before a ends at 20:30, and a starts before c ends. Both conditions hold, so they overlap.

takeaway: Tables are fixed; reservations are intervals in time on one table.

starters: Why is TimeSlot a value object and not an entity?
Should seating length depend on party size?
How would I model two tables pushed together?
